svg.text: CVA6 Fixed-Latency Unit (FLU) Divider Structural Write-Back Contention (Cycles 325 – 349)
Demonstration of the Fixed-Latency Unit writeback bottleneck: during serial division (DIV and REM), flu_ready_o is pulled LOW, asserting fu_busy_alu=1 and stalling independent ALU instructions.
Microarchitectural Insight: The Fixed-Latency Unit Structural Hazard

1. Structural Contention: At cycle 326, DIV x18 starts calculation. SerDivState enters DIVIDE (1), and MultReady drops to 0. This forces flu_ready_o=0 and FuBusyAlu=1, which freezes the issue stage for independent instruction ADDI x19, 500 until cycle 333 (DivValid=1).

2. Contrast with Pipelined Multiplier: At cycle 346, MUL x23 issues. Unlike the divider, the multiplier is fully pipelined, completing in a single cycle without de-asserting flu_ready_o or stalling subsequent operations.
